To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DEA models are very sensitive to the choice of weights, the specification of the functional forms, the treatment of environmental factors and the treatment of time effects.

(a) the choice of weights for the output measures is a crucial factor in determining the efficiency scores of the organizations; (b) the use of a stochastic frontier analysis model with a single output is not appropriate for measuring the efficiency of public service organizations; (c) the use of an appropriate statistical model is important to avoid biased estimates of efficiency scores and to allow for the effects of environmental influences and of the dynamics of performance; (d) the choice of model specification and estimation method is important
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of statistical models for measuring the performance of public service organizations and the efficiency of their resource usage.
the development of statistical methods for measuring the efficiency of public service organizations and with the use of these methods for policy analysis.

the use of efficiency measurement tools to assess the efficiency of public service organizations and, in particular, the use of these methods to assess the efficiency performance of public service organizations over a period of time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while DEA and SFA can be useful for the purposes of policy making, the results of such analyses are only as good as the data that go into them.
DEA and SFA are useful tools for measuring efficiency of public services.
the use of efficiency models in the public sector is still at an experimental stage and that the results of such models should be treated with caution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are not convinced that the current state of development of efficiency measurement methods is sufficiently mature for them to be used as the basis for regulatory decision making.
the paper is a critical review of the literature on efficiency measurement in public services.
we have shown that the use of DEA and SFA models to measure the efficiency of public sector organizations is fraught with problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

efficiency measurement models are not a panacea for the problem of measuring the efficiency of public service organizations and that the use of these models should not be seen as an end in itself, but rather as a tool to support a wider range of analysis.
the choice of model and the treatment of the model's parameters are important issues for policy makers and regulators of public services.

the efficiency of public service organizations is difficult to measure and that the measurement is sensitive to the assumptions that are made about the nature of the public services that are being provided.
